coverage.note: structural coverage (paper Def 10): a node is covered when it is in the annotations and all its outgoing edges are; leaf exits feed junction edges that only the compositions and the root hold, so leaves alone cannot cover their exits

structures.name: S1
structures.title: 1/4/7/9 structure (mechanism unknown)
structures.hypothesis: 1/4/7/9 structure (mechanism unknown): Correlates with 1s, 4s, 7s and 9s; mechanism unknown: no image rule explains it within digits (closest: a tall vertical stem, s = +0.60). It fires on 1s (87%), 4s (65%), 7s (63%) and 9s (51%). Evidence: Overall s = +0.60; within digits s = +0.47 on average over 7 digits; with the amount of ink held fixed, r = +0.03; add_stem edit: +0.31 SD against its control (as predicted).

structures.name: S2
structures.title: 4-vs-6 separator (S2)
structures.hypothesis: 4-vs-6 separator (S2): Combines S2.1 (No-stem detector (S2.1)), S2.2 (No-stem detector · with a horizontal bar along the top (S2.2)) and S2.3 (No-stem detector · with a horizontal bar along the top (S2.3)). S2.1 feeds S2.2; S2.2 feeds S2.3. Together they separate 4s from 6s (84% balanced accuracy, cross-validated) much better than the best part alone (S2.2: 76%). Its strongest exit (map h19): it responds when the image lacks a tall vertical stem: it is held back by a long, near-vertical stroke running most of the digit's height. So it fires on 3s (92%), 2s (90%), 5s (88%), 0s (83%), 8s (72%) and 6s (57%), and on 7s that have no tall vertical stem (58% vs 4% without), and on 9s that have no tall vertical stem (70% vs 8% without). Evidence: Overall s = -0.80; within digits s = -0.70 on average over 7 digits; with the amount of ink held fixed, r = -0.40; add_stem edit: -1.46 SD against its control (as predicted).

structures.name: S4
structures.title: 3-vs-7 separator (S4)
structures.hypothesis: 3-vs-7 separator (S4): Combines S4.1 (No-right-open-upper-curve detector), S4.2 (Weak open-top (4-shape) detector · without an upper curve open to the left (S4.2)), S4.3 (No-left-open-upper-curve detector) and S4.4 (Weak open-top (4-shape) detector). S4.1 feeds S4.2 and S4.3; S4.2 feeds S4.3 and S4.4. Together they separate 3s from 7s (96% balanced accuracy, cross-validated) much better than the best part alone (S4.3: 82%). Its strongest exit (map h15): it responds to a gap that opens upwards between two strokes (the top of a 4). Within digits it is also held back by an upper curve open to the left (s = -0.38, ink-controlled r = -0.62; close_upper edit +0.75 SD as predicted; open_upper edit -0.68 SD as predicted; proven). So it fires on 6s (97%), 0s (95%), 4s (77%) and 8s (66%). Evidence: Overall s = +0.42; within digits s = +0.57 on average over 2 digits; with the amount of ink held fixed, r = +0.29. The link is weak overall (|s| = 0.42 < 0.5): read it as a tendency, not a detector. No image edit tested it (or the edit's effect was too small): supported, not proven.

annotations.name: root
annotations.title: Digit scores from the structures
annotations.hypothesis: Digit scores from the structures: Reads the structures' exits through the ten score maps and the head: each score map is a sum of kernels on the exits (and on the image directly), averaged over the map, and the head mixes the ten averages into the class scores (exact, linear). The largest direct push towards each image's own digit (score margin over the mean score, on images of that digit): '0' by 3-vs-7 separator (S5) (+11.38); '1' by 3-vs-7 separator (S4) (+9.55); '2' by 3-vs-7 separator (S5) (+11.28); '3' by No-stem detector · with a horizontal bar along the top (S7) (+5.59); '4' by 3-vs-7 separator (S4) (+9.75); '5' by 3-vs-7 separator (S4) (+10.75); '6' by 3-vs-7 separator (S4) (+18.63); '7' by the image directly (+7.30); '8' by Lower-loop detector (+12.94); '9' by Lower-loop detector (+6.91).

suggester.method: attribution flow (gradient x input per edge, all class scores) + activation similarity (r >= 0.8); greedy merging that keeps the groups a DAG (5-8 structures); sub-parts by the same score inside each structure (at most 4 maps each)
